mentions.name: RSOLV
mentions.description: This tool acts as a verification layer on top of existing static security scanners, taking a highly opinionated test-driven development approach to proving (or disproving) scanner-indicated codebase vulnerabilities. It writes red tests against the desired secure behavior so that shipped fixes actually work and the customer's suite has regression protection.
mentions.problem: Customers can't trust scanner-indicated vulnerabilities or fixes without verification that they aren't causeless code mutations and that shipped fixes actually work.
mentions.source_excerpt: https://rsolv.dev takes a highly opinionated TDD approach to _proving_ (or disproving!) scanner-indicated codebase vulnerabilities and writing red tests against the desired secure behavior, so that customers can trust that they're not just making code mutations without cause, and that the shipped fixes actually work, and that there's regression protection in their suite.

evidence.value: https://rsolv.dev takes a highly opinionated TDD approach to _proving_ (or disproving!) scanner-indicated codebase vulnerabilities and writing red tests against the desired secure behavior, so that customers can trust that they're not just making code mutations without cause, and that the shipped fixes actually work, and that there's regression protection in their suite.
evidence.author: Arubis

mentions.name: rsolv
mentions.description: A security scanner that uses AST validation to reduce false positives and employs a heavily orchestrated LLM to write unit tests that fail if the detected vulnerability is present. It is in early days and open to alpha users at no cost.
mentions.problem: Security scans suffer from high false positive rates.
mentions.source_excerpt: Been hacking on https://rsolv.dev. It's a security scanner with a couple of unique twists; in addition to using AST validation to cut the false positive rate, it uses a heavily orchestrated LLM to write unit tests that fail if the detected vulnerability is present.

evidence.value: Been hacking on https://rsolv.dev. It's a security scanner with a couple of unique twists; in addition to using AST validation to cut the false positive rate, it uses a heavily orchestrated LLM to write unit tests that fail if the detected vulnerability is present.
